_comment: TEMPLATE ONLY -- this committed file is NEVER passed directly to `claude -p`
and carries NO real secrets. `crates/rdpilot-mcp/tests/live_capstone.rs`
(PROOF-04) reads this template at RUN TIME and renders a CONCRETE copy to a
gitignored std::env::temp_dir() path, substituting the tokens below, before
passing THAT rendered temp file to `claude -p --mcp-config <temp path>`:
__RDPILOT_MCP_BIN__   -> env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_rdpilot-mcp") (the compiled
rdpilot-mcp server binary this test built)
__RDPILOT_HOST__      -> .secrets/connection.json `host`
__RDPILOT_PORT__      -> .secrets/connection.json `rdpPort` (stringified;
defaults to "3389" when absent)
__RDPILOT_USERNAME__  -> .secrets/connection.json `user`
__RDPILOT_PASSWORD__  -> .secrets/connection.json `password`
__RDPILOT_SENSOR_BINARY_PATH__ -> .secrets/sensor-build/rdpilot-sensor.exe
(live-diagnosed Plan 15-08 -- without this, the
real Connect path never deploys a sensor, so
every sensor-backed tool call times out, mirroring
the identical Plan 15-06/15-07 finding)
The rendered copy's `env` block carries the REAL connection secrets for the
spawned `rdpilot-mcp` server subprocess ONLY -- it is written to a gitignored
temp path, never printed/logged, and removed after the run (T-15-08). The
capstone LLM itself never sees a host/username/password value: they reach
the server purely as ITS OWN process environment and are resolved through
the existing file->env->MCP-init layered config pipeline (D-27,
`rdpilot_config::resolve`, consumed by `rdpilot_connect`'s handler) -- so
the capstone's task prompt never needs to mention credentials at all, and
the transcript this test parses can never contain the password by
construction.
